newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFI 15 plans annual $20-40 mln investments.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFI 15 plans annual $20-40 mln investments.

text.p: Polish National Investment Fund No 15 (NFI) "Hetman" plans to invest between $20 and $40 million in buying Polish firms every year, the president of the fund's managing company said on Wednesday.
The president of Creditanstalt-SCG Fund Management SA told a news briefing the fund wanted to buy firms from its core sectors of construction materials, food processing and mineral raw materials.

"We want to invest between $20 and $40 million annually outside the fund...we feel we are experts in the sectors which we already have, but other investment...mainly in firms from other sectors is also possible," Krzysztof Sedzikowski said.
He also said the fund wanted to sell about 14 firms of its portfolio by 2000.

Sedzikowski said the fund expected to increase its value by 10 percent in real terms every year and said in the next three years even more rapid growth was possible thanks to restructuring of old firms and buying new ones.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in some 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.
The 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme will have the opportunity to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund before they start bourse trade.
